14 of Tailwind 4’s 17 coloured 500 shades lie outside sRGB; none lie outside Display P3

Tailwind CSS 4.3.3’s theme.css writes all 286 palette shades as oklch(L C h): lightness, chroma (how far from grey) and hue angle. The v4.0 announcement says the move from rgb to oklch makes colours more vivid where sRGB had limited them. This page takes the 500 shade of the 17 coloured families. We will compare each shade with the limits of sRGB and Display P3, then show what the selected screen does when a colour lies outside its range.

  2. An sRGB screen’s edge sits at a different chroma for each colour

    The outline is the most chroma sRGB can show on each spoke.

    Each spoke is one family, labelled with its hue. The outline marks the most chroma an sRGB screen can show at that colour’s own lightness and hue, found by bisection with CSS Color 4’s sample code. The spokes are evenly spaced; the hues are not: amber to yellow is 7°, red to orange 47°.

  6. On an sRGB screen, the 11 land on its edge

    Chroma drops to the edge; indigo-300 loses most, 0.115 to 0.110.

    CSS Color 4 says a colour outside the screen’s gamut must be mapped into it. Its binary search lowers chroma at fixed lightness and hue until clipping changes the colour by under 0.02, then clips; hue moves by up to 1.5°. All 11 land on the edge. indigo-300 loses most chroma: 0.115 to 0.110.

Shade: 700 · Screen: Display P3

  1. Tailwind 4 writes each colour as lightness, chroma and hue

    Each line reads oklch(L C h); C, chroma, is distance from grey.

    Tailwind CSS 4.3.3’s theme.css writes all 286 palette shades as oklch(L C h): lightness, chroma (how far from grey) and hue angle. The v4.0 announcement says the move from rgb to oklch makes colours more vivid where sRGB had limited them. This page takes the 700 shade of the 17 coloured families. We will compare each shade with the limits of sRGB and Display P3, then show what the selected screen does when a colour lies outside its range.

    • Code, 18 lines:
      • 1: /* theme.css, v4.3.3: the 700 shades */;
      • 2: --color-red-700: oklch(50.5% 0.213 27.518);
      • 3: --color-orange-700: oklch(55.3% 0.195 38.402);
      • 4: --color-amber-700: oklch(55.5% 0.163 48.998);
      • 5: --color-yellow-700: oklch(55.4% 0.135 66.442);
      • 6: --color-lime-700: oklch(53.2% 0.157 131.589);
      • 7: --color-green-700: oklch(52.7% 0.154 150.069);
      • 8: --color-emerald-700: oklch(50.8% 0.118 165.612);
      • 9: --color-teal-700: oklch(51.1% 0.096 186.391);
      • 10: --color-cyan-700: oklch(52% 0.105 223.128);
      • 11: --color-sky-700: oklch(50% 0.134 242.749);
      • 12: --color-blue-700: oklch(48.8% 0.243 264.376);

      • 17: --color-pink-700: oklch(52.5% 0.223 3.958);
      • 18: --color-rose-700: oklch(51.4% 0.222 16.935);
    • 3 labelled values:
      • L: lightness, 0% to 100%;
      • C: chroma, 0 is grey;
      • h: hue angle, degrees.

      • Lines 17 to 209 of the file, every twelfth;
      • line.
  2. An sRGB screen’s edge sits at a different chroma for each colour

    The outline is the most chroma sRGB can show on each spoke.

    Each spoke is one family, labelled with its hue. The outline marks the most chroma an sRGB screen can show at that colour’s own lightness and hue, found by bisection with CSS Color 4’s sample code. The spokes are evenly spaced; the hues are not: violet to purple is 9°, yellow to lime 65°.

    • Radar chart: 1 curve, 17 axes from 0 to 0.35:
      • sRGB edge: 0.206 at red 28°, 0.179 at orange 38°, 0.149 at amber 49°, 0.123 at yellow 66°, 0.147 at lime 132°, 0.145 at green 150°, 0.106 at emerald 166°, 0.089 at teal 186°, 0.097 at cyan 223°, 0.12 at sky 243°, 0.289 at blue 264°, 0.283 at indigo 277°, 0.274 at violet 293°, 0.262 at purple 302°, 0.244 at fuchsia 324°, 0.211 at pink 4°, 0.206 at rose 17°.
    • Key: dark grey, sRGB edge;
    • 7 labels:
      • Distance from the centre: chroma, rings;
      • 0.05 apart.
      • Each spoke keeps its own colour’s;
      • lightness and hue, so this is not one slice;
      • of the colour space.
      • The spokes are evenly spaced; the hue;
      • angles on them are not.
  3. 14 of the 17 700 shades lie outside sRGB

    Furthest past the edge: rose-700, by 0.016 chroma.

    Tailwind’s own chroma for each colour, drawn over the edge. 14 of 17 lie outside sRGB; only blue, indigo and violet fit. At this scale the overshoot is a sliver: the furthest out in chroma, rose-700, is 0.016 past the edge.

  4. As a share of the edge, emerald-700 reaches 111.4%

    The edge is now the 100 ring; blue has most room, at 84.1%.

    The same colours, each as a percentage of the sRGB edge on its own spoke. The edge becomes the 100 ring, and every colour past it shows. emerald goes furthest, to 111.4%; blue has the most room, at 84.1%. The centre is now 50%, and the rings are 25 points apart.

  5. None of the 17 lie outside Display P3

    Closest to the P3 edge: purple-700, at 96.9% of it.

    The Display P3 edge on the same scale lies beyond sRGB’s on every spoke, from 101.1% at indigo to 139.5% at green. All 17 colours fit inside it. The closest is purple-700, at 96.9% of the P3 edge, 0.009 chroma short of it.

  6. On a Display P3 screen, all 17 show as written

    Ring 100 is now the P3 edge; sRGB’s falls to 71.7%–98.9% of it.

    Now each spoke is measured against the Display P3 edge, the new 100 ring. CSS Color 4’s gamut mapping leaves a colour inside the screen’s gamut unchanged, so a P3 screen shows all 17 as written. The sRGB edge falls to 71.7%–98.9% of P3’s; purple comes closest, at 96.9%.
